stem: When reinforcing long-term dietary teaching after transplantation, which general diet pattern aligns with standard references?

options.text: A healthy diet low in fat, sugar, and salt and high in fiber
A diet unrestricted in fat, sugar, and salt for all recipients indefinitely
Complete elimination of all carbohydrates after discharge
No dietary guidance is needed once immunosuppression is stable

explanation.rationale_correct: Diet teaching encourages a healthy diet low in fat, sugar, and salt and high in fiber, while recognizing that early restrictions may be individualized during recovery.

rationale_incorrect.B: Long-term guidance emphasizes limiting fat, sugar, and salt rather than unrestricted intake for all recipients.
rationale_incorrect.C: Fiber and balanced nutrition are encouraged rather than eliminating all carbohydrates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Diet recommendations continue to be reinforced as recovery progresses.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → d. Diet → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Encourage a healthy diet low in fat, sugar and salt and high in fiber

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → d. Diet → ii. (healthy diet low in fat, sugar, and salt; high in fiber); PDF p. 115 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. General healthy-diet angle distinct from hand-hygiene teaching (cctc-1019, p. 115) and raw-egg precautions (cctc-1119); anchor verified on Cupples p. 115.

stem: A warehouse worker preparing to return to employment after transplant asks about job-specific precautions. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Assess work activities for suitability and discuss potential restrictions such as weightlifting and exposure to toxic agents
Return-to-work planning never considers occupational exposures
All recipients must resume prior heavy labor without assessment
Toxic occupational exposures are encouraged to build stamina

explanation.rationale_correct: Return-to-work counseling includes assessing work activities for suitability and discussing potential restrictions such as weightlifting and exposure to toxic agents along with required precautions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Work activities and exposures are specifically assessed rather than ignored.
rationale_incorrect.C: Return timing and restrictions depend on recovery and job demands rather than automatic resumption of heavy labor.
rationale_incorrect.D: Toxic exposures may require restrictions rather than being encouraged.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → n. Return to work → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Assess patient's work activities to determine suitability; discuss potential restrictions (e.g., weightlifting; exposure to toxic agents)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → n. Return to work → iii. (assess work activities; weightlifting and toxic-agent restrictions); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Work-restriction angle distinct from telework/part-time counseling (cctc-3059) and return-to-work combo (cctc-1133); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: When a transplant recipient cannot safely return to previous employment, which referral aligns with standard return-to-work references?

options.text: Refer to Social Worker or Vocational Rehabilitation
Discharge planning ends with no vocational resources
Refer only to an unrelated subspecialty surgeon
Permanent unemployment is the only supported outcome

explanation.rationale_correct: When patients should not return to previous employment, references direct referral to Social Worker or Vocational Rehabilitation for vocational support.

rationale_incorrect.B: Vocational resources are available through social work and vocational rehabilitation referral.
rationale_incorrect.C: Vocational rehabilitation and social work—not unrelated surgical referral—is the cited pathway.
rationale_incorrect.D: Alternative employment planning is supported rather than assuming permanent unemployment.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → n. Return to work → iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Refer patients to Social Worker or Vocational Rehabilitation if patients should not return to their previous employment

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → n. Return to work → iv. (Social Worker or Vocational Rehabilitation referral); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Vocational-referral angle distinct from work-restriction assessment (cctc-1131) and heart return-to-work telework item (cctc-3059); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: A coordinator is updating return-to-work teaching materials. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Patients may be counseled to initially telework or work part-time and gradually increase to full-time employment as energy improves.
Work activities should be assessed for suitability, including potential restrictions such as weightlifting and toxic exposures.
All recipients must return to their previous full-time job without assessment or modification.
Patients who should not return to previous employment may be referred to Social Worker or Vocational Rehabilitation.

explanation.rationale_correct: Gradual return, work-activity assessment with restrictions, and vocational referral are supported. Statement III is false because return-to-work planning is individualized rather than mandating unmodified return to prior full-time employment.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—vocational rehabilitation referral is cited when prior employment is unsuitable.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because work suitability and restrictions are assessed.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → n. Return to work
primary_anchor.quote_hint: telework or work part-time … gradually increase … Assess patient's work activities … weightlifting … toxic agents … Social Worker or Vocational Rehabilitation

references.locator: Ch. 3 → n. Return to work → ii.–iv. (gradual return, work restrictions, vocational referral); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
